author: olivier0407
text: My experience with 007 First Light was a huge disappointment, turning what should have been a grand secret agent adventure into a complete technical and ergonomic nightmare. Right from the start, the game showed its limits with a sloppy level of polish, highlighted by major bugs like a total crash during the opening cinematic. My progress quickly hit broken scripts, particularly during the training sessions in Q's lab where targets failed to respawn, completely trapping me in the area and forcing me to reload my save. On top of that, the objective guidance is disastrous, forcing me to wander aimlessly just to find absurd narrative triggers like a broken phone hidden in a restroom, while the endless load times after every death finished off whatever patience I had **** terms of gameplay, the title markets itself as a modern experience when it actually delivers archaic and ultra-rigid stealth. Far from the freedom I expect from a Hitman game, it locks me into strict corridors. The artificial intelligence relies on stationary guards with overlapping lines of sight straight out **** from fifteen years ago, making even the slightest attempt at improvisation instantly punitive. This rigidity extends to my character's movement, as he is unable to jump or crawl under obstacles during the boat sequence unless prompted by a contextual action, while the climbing phases are fully automated and utterly **** action sequences fail to save the experience and proved to be just as frustrating. Gunfights boil down to pushing through brutal walls of bullets where I die in seconds, made worse by a ridiculous scarcity of ammunition that forces me to constantly scavenge corpses, along with an absurd "permission to fire" mechanic. Hand-to-hand combat is heavy, clunky, and imprecise, leaving me running around in a panic looking for any random object to throw at enemies. As for my gadget arsenal, my secret agent fantasy was **** by the ridiculous requirement to rummage through trash cans and drawers for batteries or chemicals—an artificial looting mechanic designed solely to limit my gear and force me into using the Bluff system, a tedious dialogue mini-game that destroys the pace of the **** immersion was further ruined by an unlikable cast and setting. The writing turns MI6 into a toxic workplace where my boss, M, spends his time barking orders and belittling me over the comms, while Moneypenny loses all her charm to become an annoying nag. Even the vehicle sequences, which should be a staple of the franchise, suffer from a complete lack of feedback and are an absolute **** breaking point came during the warehouse sequence. Pinned down under relentless enemy fire, given no clear direction, and worn out by my character repeating the exact same hint line on a loop, I simply had enough. This accumulation of poor design, constant frustration, and outdated mechanics wrapped in empty marketing hype made my decision easy: I quit the game on the spot and permanently uninstalled a title that has nothing to offer beyond an empty marketing shell.

author: SkillPoint
text:
Mit 007 First Light beweisen die Entwickler von IO Interactive eindrucksvoll, dass das James-Bond-Franchise auch abseits der Leinwand zu absoluten Höchstformen auflaufen kann. Die fesselnde und hervorragend gespielte Origin-Story füllt eine spannende Lücke im Leben des Geheimagenten, während das gelungene Leveldesign im besten Sinne an die spielerische Freiheit der Hitman-Reihe erinnert. Einzig die phasenweise sehr langen, actionlastigen Schusspassagen im „John Wick“-Stil kratzen hin und wieder leicht an der eleganten Spionage-Atmosphäre. Wer jedoch einen packenden, wunderschön inszenierten und spielerisch abwechslungsreichen Agenten-Thriller sucht, wird mit diesem Abenteuer meisterhaft bedient.

author: Mxmax914
text: I played James Bond First Light on PlayStation 5 Pro, and as someone who has always enjoyed the James Bond franchise, both through the classic films and most of the video games, I had a really good time with **** has been a long time since we had a proper James Bond video game, and First Light does a good job of bringing back the feeling of the franchise. The story uses many of the classic Bond ingredients: conspiracies, betrayals, high-level tension within MI6, varied missions and a strong spy atmosphere. At times, it really feels like playing through an interactive Bond movie, which works very well for this kind of **** gameplay feels natural and enjoyable. The game moves between platforming, stealth, action and driving sequences, which keeps the pacing fresh. The vehicle sections are also quite fun and add some welcome variety. I liked the way the game constantly switches between different types of gameplay while still feeling coherent.Visually, the game is more uneven. Some scenes look really good, with nice environments and strong cinematic direction. However, there is also some clipping, textures sometimes appear late, and a few visual details lack polish. It is not a major issue, but it does prevent the game from feeling technically excellent.I finished the game over a few evenings, playing sessions of around one and a half to two hours, and I genuinely enjoyed the experience. It is a fully single-player, cinematic adventure, and honestly, it feels good to play something like this without competition, online pressure or multiplayer systems.That being said, replay value is quite limited. Once finished, I did not really feel a strong reason to start it again immediately. It is more the kind of game you may replay years later with some nostalgia, like rewatching a good action **** is not game of the year material, but it is a very enjoyable experience and a successful tribute to the James Bond franchise. A solid and entertaining return for Bond in video game form.

author: Phil8707
text:
Hier ist die nochmals feingeschliffene Fassung. Ich habe die Kritik an der fehlenden deutschen Sprachausgabe (und den damit verbundenen Untertiteln im Gameplay) nahtlos in den Block zur Inszenierung und Atmosphäre eingebaut:
Rezension: [007 First light] – Ein starkes Fundament mit Agentenschwächen
Eine wirklich schöne Story, die sich hervorragend in das bekannte 007-Universum einbettet. Man lernt zusammen mit Bond die typischen Aufgaben, Kniffe und Mechaniken seiner Spionage-Karriere von der Pike auf kennen. Getragen wird das Ganze von einer fantastischen Grafik und einer dichten, eleganten Inszenierung, die den Geist der Filme perfekt einfängt – vom exzellenten Sounddesign bis hin zu den detailverliebten, luxuriösen Schauplätzen. Auch das Pacing zwischen ruhigen Schleichpassagen und packenden Sequenzen stimmt. Ein Wermutstropfen für die Atmosphäre ist allerdings das komplette Fehlen einer deutschen Sprachausgabe. Wer der englischen Sprache nicht absolut mächtig ist, muss permanent Untertitel mitlesen, was gerade in dynamischen Gameplay-Momenten ablenkt und der filmischen Immersion schadet.
Abzüge gibt es zudem bei der Inszenierung der Action. Die KI ist schlicht zu einfach gestrickt und agiert in Schusswechseln oft kopflos. Zudem wirken die Schusssequenzen durch die allzu plump und auffällig platzierten roten Fässer oder freiliegenden Leitungen arg konstruiert. Hier fehlt es dem Spieldesign an Subtilität; die Umgebungen schreien dem Spieler die Interaktionsmöglichkeiten förmlich entgegen, statt zum cleveren Experimentieren einzuladen.
Die unverkennbaren Hitman-Wurzeln der Entwickler sind spürbar, wurden hier jedoch spürbar vereinfacht. Das tut dem Spielfluss grundsätzlich gut, da es den Fokus weg vom reinen Sandbox-Puzzle hin zu einer geradlinigeren Agenten-Erfahrung verlagert und dem Spiel eine eigene Identität verleiht. Gelegentlich führt diese Vereinfachung aber auch zu einem recht starren Leveldesign, das einem wenig kreativen Spielraum lässt. Während die Umgebungen optisch glänzen, wirken manche Charakteranimationen in den Cutscenes zudem etwas hölzern.
Die Eskalationsmissionen sind eine nette Dreingabe für zwischendurch, fallen vom Umfang her aber noch viel zu gering aus. Auch das Missionsdesign **** hier: Einige spielerische Ideen und Aufgaben sind durchaus interessant, andere wiederum wirken eher bemüht oder gar blöd gelöst.
Fazit: Das spielerische und atmosphärische Fundament steht. Wenn das Team für den Nachfolger die KI anzieht, die Umgebungsrätsel subtiler gestaltet, eine vollständige Lokalisierung spendiert und den Mut zu mehr spielerischer Freiheit hat, erwartet uns ein absolutes Highlight. Ich bin definitiv gespannt, was das Team aus Teil 2 macht.

author: CordellTaylor
text: I have not been so invested in a 007 game since Agent Under Fire and GoldenEye, but this? This just does it for me. This isn't just a game. This is 007. This is James Bond. YOU are James Bond. The agent. The playboy. The debonair. Many games go for that "feels-like-a-movie" vibe, but IO Interactive puts on a master class performance with this production.  Celebrity cameos from Gemma Chan, Kenny Kravitz, etc., immaculate world building taking you on an international espionage-laced journey, beautiful women, beautiful set pieces, iconic gadgets, nods to cinema, the Lana Del Rey opening number, etc. Everything about 007 First Light is what James Bond should be. Not to mention how well written and portrayed every character is. Whether they're as brief as Cressida Bright or as extensive as Greenway and Moneypenny, and of course, Patrick Gibson's James Bond, everything feels valuable. Looking forward to making different choices and taking alternate routes that I didn't in my first playthrough, because this game encourages replayability, and so do I. My second 10/10 this year, and well deserved. I hope Hollywood sees what myself and many others do. Patrick Gibson is worthy of taking on the role of James Bond on the big screen.

author: tYsU
text:
Ogółem gra jest bardzo dobra, ale jest parę rzeczy, które są niedopracowane, lub dla mnie są minusami. 

Graficznie gra stoi na bardzo dobrym poziomie, ale na PS5 Pro niektóre tekstury to jest jakaś tragedia, istna pikseloza - niektóre elementy podłogi, albo zdjęcia, czy też napisy, itd. Jest to w sumie losowe, ale czytałem, że to faktycznie jest problem nie tylko na PS5.

Jeżeli chodzi o muzykę i audio jak dla mnie jest super i nie mam zastrzeżeń.

System walki wręcz mimo wszystko nie jest jakoś bardzo rozbudowany. Myślę, że mogli wykonać lepszą robotę, jeżeli chodzi o więcej kombinacji jeżeli chodzi o klawisze, bo aktualnie to jest kwestia wciskania dwóch guzików, lub spamowanie jednego. Wizualnie wygląda to dobrze, ale jeżeli chodzi o trudność, czy moje odczucia to mogłoby być lepiej. 

Bardzo drewniany model jazdy. Rozumiem, że nie na tym w tej grze się skupiamy i to tylko mały dodatek, ale mimo wszystko jest mega drewniany. Mało swobody ma gracz, jeżeli chodzi o prowadzenie pojazdu, responsywność jest słaba w kwestii gazu, czy skręcania w niektórych pojazdach.

Jeżeli chodzi o postęp w grze, to nie za bardzo podoba mi się fakt późnego dostania pistoletu z tłumikiem, bo jest to praktycznie w połowie gry. Preferowałbym go dostać od razu na początku i działać mega po cichu, ale niestety tak się nie da. Na początku również ograniczają zasób gadżetów, co rozumiem, ale preferowałbym możliwość wykorzystania wszystkich 4 gniazd do ich osadzenia. 

Samo strzelanie jest w porządku, ale dosyć bruździ tutaj fakt, że gdy jest ostra zadyma, to trzeba się skupiać na podnoszeniu broni i amunicji z przeciwników, bo ta bardzo szybko się kończy. Amunicja uzupełnia się dopiero, jak znajdziemy taką samą broń, a przeciwnicy walczą różną, wiec co chwila trzeba ją zmieniać.
Dosyć upierdliwe jest też ciągłe szukanie chemikaliów i urządzeń, aby ładować pasek gadżetów. W sensie rozumiem, że to jest mechanika gry, ale jest to dosyć monotonne i na pewno jakieś inne rozwiązanie mogłoby być lepsze. 

Przydałaby się jakaś osobna sala treningowa, aby mieć możliwość potrenowania sobie bez pośpiechu, bo fabuła ciągnie nas przez szkolenie, ale ono jest zbyt chaotyczne. W sensie nie ma możliwości powtórzenia na spokojnie tych rzeczy, tylko od razu przechodzisz z jednego mechanizmu na drugi. 

Symulacje taktyczne to jak dla mnie lekki nie wypał. W sensie nie za bardzo czuje chęć i potrzebę przechodzenia tego w ogóle. Nie wiem czego to kwestia, ale prawdopodobnie tego, że jest to bardzo powtarzalne, bo jak się przeszło już fabułę, to te lokacje się zna i to trochę zniechęca. Możliwe, że gdyby były one nowe, unikalne było by lepiej. Wprowadzenie losowości na pewno by urozmaiciło ten tryb.

Gra czasami jest zbyt łatwa. Nie ma tutaj za dużo takich przerywników w postaci, np. quick time eventów. Występują one praktycznie na samym końcu gry i polegają na wciśnięciu tego samego przycisku 3 razy. Dużo lepiej by tutaj sprawdziło się dodanie ich podczas wspinaczki, lub przemieszczania się w różnych lokacjach, lub też przy przesuwaniu rzeczy, itd. Tego mi brakowało, takiej większej ilości interakcji i wpływu na to co robimy.
Boli mnie trochę, że producenci nadal nie wykorzystują możliwości jakie daje Dual Sense, czy inne pady. Żyroskop, touchpad, mikrofon, itd. Użycie tych funkcji wzmocniło by znacznie odczucia z gry.

Krótki wątek z Bawmą. Po takim wprowadzeniu myślałem, że jednak będziemy mieć więcej do czynienia z nim. Rozczarowało mnie to, że po tym jak się wisiało nad krokodylami od razu był taki przeskok i praktycznie żadnej konwersacji z nim, ale wiemy, że będzie w DLC, więc mam nadzieję, że ten wątek zostanie nadrobiony.

Błędów jako tako za dużo nie doświadczyłem, ale czasami postać mimo wciskania klawiszu uniku i tak otrzymywała obrażenia. Było również pojedyncze zablokowanie się NPC na szafce.

Klimat bardzo mi się podobał. Bardzo piękne lokacje, różnorodne. Widać, że one żyją własnym życiem, są interakcje z NPCami i między nimi też dużo dialogów, które są ciekawe i przyjemnie się ich słucha.

Fabularnie nie mam się do czego przyczepić, szału nie było, ale tragedii też.

Pierwszoplanowe postacie odgrywały bardzo dobrze, przyjemnie się je oglądało i słuchało, mimika była w porządku. Miałem wątpliwości co do głównego bohatera, bo wiem, że przed premierą opinie były mieszane, ale dla mnie wybór tego aktora był jak najbardziej na plus. 

Ogólna moja ocena to 7/10 ale bardziej kierowałbym się na 7,5/10. Jest parę minusów i wad, ale w ogólnym rozrachunku bardzo przyjemnie spędziłem czas grając w tą produkcje.

author: Phaasm
text: Bought this game because of all the hype and overwhelmingly positive reviews. Unfortunately, I regret it—honestly, I’m still frustrated with myself for falling for it.I expected something like a refined “Hitman” experience set in the Bond universe. That’s not what this is. Nothing here really stands out as better. The graphics are decent, but that’s about it. The story isn’t terrible, but it’s far from engaging. It follows a very typical Bond formula where the villain is always closer than you think, but it never manages to feel **** gameplay is extremely basic and, frankly, not enjoyable. You’re given almost no freedom in how to approach missions. Everything feels linear and restrictive. Even compared to Uncharted—which isn’t an open-world game—you feel significantly more freedom there than you do in First **** AI is disappointing, easily worse than what you’d find in most Hitman **** of the most frustrating aspects is the gadget system. The watch mechanics feel tedious, constantly forcing you to recharge it using random electronic objects scattered around. On top of that, collecting chemical products adds nothing meaningful to the experience. It feels like unnecessary filler.James Bond is supposed to have a license to kill, yet about 75% of the time you’re forced into hand-to-hand combat. It gets repetitive very quickly.I was already bored after 15 minutes, hoping it would improve—but it never did.After spending $100 CAD, I honestly feel misled. It makes me question how genuine those glowing reviews really were. Amazon has a lot of money, and it’s hard not to wonder.Verdict: Don’t buy it. You’ll likely get bored fast.

author: ifgram
text:
Not THAT good.

A mix of Hitman and Uncharted that only succeeds in wanting me to play those other games. The Hitman-esque open world sections are far too narrow and guided, completely losing the feeling of endless possibilities and replay-ability of the most recent trilogy. Uncharted style puzzle sections feel like a slog, not particularly challenging, and slow to get through simply because bond is locked at a snail’s walking pace. The hand to hand combat is fun, but once you get a gun, it’s too easy to simply headshot everyone, making you completely ditch the melee/gadgets. Even on Hard mode.

The resources system is painfully frustrating, and On multiple occasions, I found myself aimlessly walking around the map looking for chemical or electronic resources to get past a certain part, and at some points even restarting checkpoints to get my resources back because you absolutely need certain gadgets to get past certain parts. It all disincentivizes the use of gadgets in a very frustrating way. 

The story may very well be the saving grace of the whole thing. While not mind blowing, the core relationships are solid, and I found myself empathizing with a more characterized and fleshed out Bond than often appears in the films. However, I am extremely bored with the aesthetic of high tech capers like this. The magic and fun of bond are the cheesy gadgets, the over the top villains with often times ludicrous plans. With such a grounded story, I found the central plot to be very typical of any other espionage franchise following corruption and technology. It may be a contemporary take, but it doesn’t exactly feel as fun as the early films.

Uncharted 4 came out a decade ago. Same with the first Hitman remake. It’s remarkable to me that this game feels regressed from these by a fair amount. I feel the hype has a lot to do with the character and our hunger for simple, single player adventures like this. 

The basis is here, I just hope the team sees this first entry as a launchpad for sequels that can match or surpass the level of it’s inspirations, instead of feeling like a watered down mixture of them all.

author: TeaBoyy
text:
I think the most redeeming quality of this game is the overarching narrative. The wider plot contains thoughtful political intrigue, smokescreens, and espionage. Despite this, I think the writing falls short in the moment-to-moment aspects as it focuses on the more superficial connections and the sarcastic adolescent quips that are poorly delivered throughout. You know what they say about sarcasm, right? If you don't, then fear not, for you will certainly come to know by the end of the game, as every character has sarcasm woven into their DNA!Additionally, the narrative greatly struggles with pacing, with the initial third of the game moving too fast and final third being slow as molasses. This impacts character relationships, perceptions, and value. 

Gameplay is a major weak point for First Light. From melee combat, to gunfights, to driving, to stealthing, it is done at a sub-par level. The gameplay aspects have been executed in one of the most uninspired ways possible. I am sincerely disappointed because there is literally nothing that has been refined nor innovated upon. The enemy intelligence is lacklustre, the NPC behaviour is dumb as bricks, and the set pieces are dull imitations. 

-Melee combat may be crunchy, but it is underwhelming and bland. By the 2nd or 3rd mission, you will already have seen all melee combat animations/combos, stealth takedowns animations, and enemy types. By the 4th mission or so, you will have experienced the only unique fighting style and situation. Where is the refinement and/or innovation? They could have taken ideas from many different enemy types from the likes of Batman, God of War, Elden Ring, Spiderman, Dishonored, Uncharted, Mad Max, Assassins Creed, Yakuza, and I am sure a plethora of others. 

-The state of melee combat is compounded by a few things. As mentioned earlier, the FOV being far too close makes for a frustratingly claustrophobic experience. At times it can feel worse than Elden Ring, and even then, you can give that game a pass because you are slaying behemoths. 

-More often than not, fisticuffs take place in tight spaces with no lock on. No lock on is not that big of an issue, but it can get annoying if the camera is uncooperative.

-Immersion breaking ‘stealth’ takedowns. No choke holds or neck snapping. Straight up, judo tossing or smashing faces into inanimate objects before throat punching or face smashing. Crickets. 

-Reloading chemical weapons with hand sanitisers……would be funny in a Johnny English video game world. Not here though. 

-Guns lack oomph. Faster to dispatch enemies hand-to-hand. Aiming feels shoddy too. 

-Poorly implemented cover system. Splinter Cell: Blacklist, Uncharted, The Last of Us, all do it better.

-Clunky and erratic movement. Inconsistent jogging to sprinting, cover to cover does not feel smooth, Bond suddenly jumps up like a gazelle and sprints. Transitioning cover to cover in gunfights is also poorly implemented as you can be stuck in crouch mode. When sprinting during gunfights Bond’s agility skyrockets.

 -Forced walking sections with no auto walk or hold to walk. 



Decent graphics and wonderful use of lighting. Nothing outstanding here though. Optimisation is not up to scratch but that is an industry wide problem. Smoke grenades and driving fast really tanked my FPS and caused stutters. Poor audio design in my opinion too. During combat set pieces the music is over-powering and combined with explosions and such you can barely hear the dialogue. It really is a bit of a racket. There are also times during stealth or investigation where there is no music at all which feels off. 

A ridiculous amount of platforming that is nowhere near as exhilarating or visually impressive as other single player games like Tomb Raider and Uncharted. -Level design was talked about having multiple approaches, but these changes in approach are so small that it doesn’t feel like it at all. If you have experienced top notch level design from franchises like Deus Ex, MGS, Dishonored, Splinter Cell, and Prey then you will be thoroughly unimpressed here. 

-Bond is not charming at all. They keep saying he is, but the game suffers from not showing just telling. Nathan Drake would actually make a better Bond. -Greenway is a miserable git. Berates Bond whenever he can and shushes Bond for no reason during missions. Even after you find about his ordeal, you really do not warm up to him.

author: SewAwOw
text:
Классный боевик про молодого Бонда. Авторам удалось соблюсти баланс между нелинейностью хитмана и зрелищностью анчартед. Игра выглядит хорошо, может, не самый топ по графике, но современно и имеет хорошую оптимизацию. Плюс имеется хорошо проработанная физика объектов окружения, что на самом деле редкость в подобным играх.
Геймплейно она тяготеет к похождениям лысого убийцы, у нас есть обширные уровни с несколькими маршрутами, и мы вольны сами выбирать как проходить их - по стелсу, используя разнообразные гаджеты и предметы окружения, или в лобовую, отстреливаясь за укрытиями. Интеллект врагов неплохой, тела своих товарищей замечают издалека, стреляют довольно метко, покидывают гранаты, умеют обходить с флангов. Хотя часто не слышат шум буквально в паре метров от себя, но мб это уже условности. Прокачки нет вообще, что плюс, только гаджеты от Q и смекалка. Стрелять приятно, стрелять дают не всегда, поэтому Бонд умеет хорошо драться, к тому же владеет разными приёмчиками вроде подзывания врагов или их забалтывания. 
Сюжетно это какбы приквел ко всем фильмам серии, нам показывают становление Бонда как агента (еще без номера 007), как он вообще попал в МИ6, его первое знакомство с М и Q. Ну и отношения с женщинами, куда без них.
Как по мне, это лучшая игра во франшизе, в ней всё на своих местах.

author: ChefD7_
text:
Ce propose une aventure spectaculaire, portée par une excellente mise en scène et une ambiance digne des meilleurs films d'espionnage. L’histoire est prenante, avec plusieurs moments forts et une vraie dose d’émotion qui rendent le scénario agréable à suivre.
Les mécaniques de gameplay sont efficaces et les gunfights offrent de bonnes sensations. Les combats au corps-à-corps sont également une vraie réussite, avec des animations variées et des enchaînements dynamiques qui rendent chaque affrontement agréable. 
En revanche, les combats deviennent assez répétitifs au fil de l’aventure, et le manque de munitions oblige constamment à ramasser les armes des ennemis, ce qui casse souvent le rythme de l’action.
Le plus gros défaut reste l’absence de doublage français. Dans un jeu aussi dynamique, où l’attention est principalement portée sur le gameplay, il est difficile de lire les sous-titres en permanence. Les joueurs non bilingues risquent donc de passer à côté d’une grande partie de l’histoire, des dialogues et de certains éléments importants du scénario.
Enfin, un sprint un peu plus rapide aurait été apprécié, les déplacements entre les différents objectifs pouvant parfois sembler trop longs et casser le rythme de l’exploration. 
Malgré ces défauts, 007 First Light reste une très bonne expérience, grâce à son ambiance, sa mise en scène et son scénario captivant.

author: skogsgurka
text: What a ride, I’m so incredibly pleased with this game. It was a tall order for IOI to mix Uncharted & Hitman while simultaneously depicting a James Bond worthy of his name. But they really served that cocktail shaken, not stirred. It’s got witty writing, a perfect main actor, excellent pacing, frantic combat, skillful combat, and sneaky stealth. It’s very linear, which felt good and is necessary to achieve the excellent pacing. But the combat would occasionally confuse me whether it was okay to improvise, or absolutely not. Shorter loading times would’ve made this less problematic. The shooting was initially difficult for me, but once I improved my headshot skills it was a blast, it just wasn’t very clear that I really needed to master that technique at first. Wish the gauntlets would allow for more improvisation; flinging my gun into someone’s face, then rushing them hand to hand, stealing their gun and continuing the fight. Those were some of the best moments and I wanted more of it! The stealth bits worked great as a contrast to the action, and the bluff mechanic is a truly genius way to make Bond’s witty personality interactive! But I’m not a fan of stealth when it becomes a monotonous routine, and overusage of the Q-Watch was a problem for me. I struggle with Hitman’s general stealth mechanics too, and just like in Hitman I think it works best when it’s actually less systemic and more like a linear puzzle with a number of spectacular murder mystery solutions.Storywise, it does a good job even though I personally found it difficult to follow all the details. I got the broad strokes and was satisfied but perhaps not as entangled as **** technical aspects of the game are incredible on the audio visual side, outstanding work. But I had several crashes, a corrupted save file, the loading times really are jarringly long, and I’m missing a manual save system which I think is paramount in a stealth game. After finishing it I went back and played some of the best parts again, and doing that when I’d mastered the systems was an incredible experience. Would’ve been a 9/10 if that was my first run!

author: Davicin49
text: 007 First Light is, above all, a James Bond film turned into a video game. It does not try to reinvent anything or revolutionize the genre, and in fact it borrows recognizable ideas from other action, stealth, and cinematic adventure titles. However, it combines them with such rhythm and precision that the result works wonderfully. It is one of those games that understands exactly what it wants to be: a direct, spectacular experience packed with moments designed to keep the player constantly engaged.Across its approximately 15-hour campaign, 007 First Light delivers a very well-paced experience, with a clearly cinematic structure and a constant succession of action scenes, infiltration sequences, and situations that feel unmistakably Bond. The sensation is that of being inside an interactive blockbuster, where every mission tries to offer something memorable and where there is rarely any room for boredom. Many of its mechanics may feel familiar from other video games, but what matters is that they are well integrated and always serve the **** of its greatest strengths lies in how it combines stealth with direct combat. The game allows many situations to be approached however the player prefers at any given moment, without making one option feel clearly wrong or giving the impression that you are playing “incorrectly”. You can move forward discreetly, use environmental resources, improvise, or resolve encounters in a more aggressive way, and in every case the experience flows naturally. That flexibility keeps the pace from ever slowing down and gives each section a constant sense of **** a technical level, 007 First Light also holds up very well. It is a visually polished game, with spectacular staging and a finish that does not fall behind current standards. Its presentation reinforces the feeling of playing through a modern spy film, with well-directed scenes, impactful action, and a rhythm that aims to deliver dopamine at every **** perhaps that is why it works so well: because it is the kind of game that feels increasingly rare nowadays. It does not invent new mechanics or reinvent the wheel, but it does aim for something we do not see often enough: being faithful to its license, being fun, and doing things right. It is the kind of single-player experience that is enjoyable from beginning to end and, precisely because it is so well paced, ends up feeling shorter than you would **** final impression is very positive. 007 First Light is not only an intense and highly entertaining cinematic adventure, but also a very promising starting point for a new line of 007 video games. Its formula has plenty of room to grow through future installments or DLCs, and it leaves the impression that, with this foundation, James Bond may finally have a modern video game series worthy of the character.

author: TitaniumDragon
text:
007 First Light is a stealth/action game.

You play as a young James Bond, the game starting out even before you become a 00 agent, on a mission where you end up attracting the attention of MI6 as a potential operative. You go through a training montage, training with other prospective 00 agents, and build some bonds with them, as well as your instructor, Greenway, who is a former 00 agent himself.

Of course, the game would not be a James Bond story if there weren’t twists and turns, and the game has a good number of plot twists. The obvious villain at the start of the game isn’t the main villain (though the actual main villain is not exactly subtle), and the game manages to take you through a variety of different locations and scenarios as you try and resolve the current crisis. It has a number of fun setpieces and you have to infiltrate a bunch of different places over the course of the story, with segments shifting between stealth, puzzle solving in more socially mingling environments, and gunplay segments where you have to blast your way through enemies and drive vehicles on chases.

The game thus alternates between these different modes to try and keep things fresh and varied, and while it works well from the perspective of mixing things up, unfortunately, it is also where the game falls down hardest.

The core of the problem is that none of these segments are particularly good – the driving is lackluster, the social mingling is decent but ends up being a bit samey over time, the stealth mechanics are pretty much the same throughout the game (use something to distract the person -> sneak past them), and the gunplay is pretty basic and repetitive, without much variety in enemies. There are a few things that mix up the gameplay a bit more, but all in all, the gameplay is really the weakest part of this game – it ends up feeling repetitive by the end of it because there just isn’t enough depth to any of the game’s mechanics.Story-wise, the story is solid enough, with fun, well-acted characters (both friend and foe) and an overall solid enough plot. James Bond is likeable, and is a bit impetuous and independent here, showing a stubborn streak. He works well enough, and the implication that there were other 00s before him (along with various easter egg references to movies/stories) is fun. Moneypenny, Q, M, Greenway, your fellow 00 recruits, and some other friends and foes are fun enough characters, and work pretty well all told.

Overall, I think this game is pretty decent, and I feel like this game does a much better job of “making you feel like James Bond” than any other 007 game ever has; this game has a lot more actual spying going on, with you engaging in social interactions and “hiding in plain sight” rather than having to sneak through every area behind waist-high walls or just blast your way through everything.

But I think the game mechanics’ shallowness holds the game back from absolute greatness.

author: TurdFerguson69
text:
First of all, let me just say that 007: First Light is a GOOD game. I enjoyed playing it and I want to be clear on that. BUT if I’m being honest it comes up just a little bit short of my expectations. Specifically the hand to hand combat is really quite basic and can be kinda janky/clunky feeling. It’s not bad, I’m not saying that at all. But for as amazing as this game LOOKS, the melee combat could (and should) be better and more in depth and it could play smoother at times. I think it could benefit from having a dedicated button like Left trigger/bumper or maybe just a simple target lock…SOMETHING that can square bond up to his enemy when fighting hand to hand. The environment is fairly interactive during combat which is good but they don’t get very creative with it, I mean, ok you can throw a guy against/into the all the stuff but typically it doesn’t result in anything that’s particularly unique or especially interesting. Idk, I’m just saying that using the surrounding environment in melee combat isn’t as awesome as it could be. But I digress, this is a minor critique. Also, I’m not saying they should’ve just copied another game but it would benefit from having more of a free-flow type of combat system like the Rocksteady Arkham games or Sleeping Dogs if you remember that game…and like I said, smoother…like more fluid looking/feeling. 

Let me remind you once again tho…its not bad by any means, the melee combat, it’s just kinda clunky and plain. I say this as a long time fan of  Hitman so I have high standards for IO’s finished product because I know how talented they are.

Also, the stealth…it’s fine. It’s ok. It could also be improved upon. I like how you use the Bond gadgets to assist with stealth but the environment is really only set up for turning things off/on so idk what but I feel like there could be more variety in that regard. Just my own personal opinion, maybe I’m alone in thinking that. 

But Ok, that’s pretty much it. Those things are really my only critiques. All in all It’s still a damn good time. It’s basically like a Bond themed Uncharted game…which is exactly what I want out of a James Bond game. Most of all, I’m really REALLY glad that they didn’t neuter the James Bond character. You know…“for the modern audience” as developers like to say…right before they are about to ruin a game out of fear of offending literally anyone. But I’m happy to report they DIDN’T! They did a great job on that front. He’s James frickin Bond alright. He’s smooth, he’s suave, he blows **** up, he drives kickass cars, he fights bad guys on top of runaway trains n **** reckless, he’s got balls the size of watermelons and he bangs beautiful women all over the planet and we love him for it, dammit! 

I officially declare that 007: First Light is a good game. It’s not great…but so what? Bottom line is that it’s a return to form for this game franchise and I for one am glad Bond is back. Really looking forward to the next installment as I expect it will surely be even bigger, better and Bondier

I score it 8 Walther PPK’s out of 10 .

author: Gabrielvsouzaa
text: 007 First Light is exactly the kind of game James Bond fans have been waiting for. Rather than simply recreating the formula established by decades of films, it successfully tells an origin story that feels fresh while remaining unmistakably Bond. It balances espionage, action, intrigue, and cinematic spectacle with remarkable confidence, creating an experience that is as enjoyable to play as it is to **** of the game's greatest achievements is its narrative. The story unfolds like a high-quality spy thriller, full of twists, memorable set pieces, and believable character development. Watching Bond evolve from a talented but inexperienced agent into the iconic secret operative we know adds genuine emotional weight to the adventure. It captures the essence of Ian Fleming's character while giving players something entirely new.Visually, the game is stunning. Every location is beautifully realized, from luxurious casinos and bustling cities to remote facilities and breathtaking landscapes. The level of detail is exceptional, making each environment feel authentic and alive. Combined with impressive lighting, facial animation, and cinematic camera work, the presentation consistently feels worthy of a blockbuster **** performances deserve enormous praise. Every major character delivers convincing and nuanced acting, helping the story maintain its momentum from beginning to end. The voice cast brings personality and credibility to every conversation, while the motion capture elevates emotional scenes far beyond what is typically expected in action games. It's one of those rare titles where dialogue feels just as engaging as the gameplay itself.Gameplay strikes an excellent balance between stealth, investigation, gadgets, gunplay, and high-octane action. Rather than forcing players into constant firefights, First Light embraces the fantasy of being a secret agent. There are multiple ways to approach objectives, rewarding careful planning as much as quick thinking. Whether infiltrating enemy compounds, gathering intelligence, or improvising during missions that inevitably spiral out of control, the game constantly makes you feel like **** pacing is another highlight. Quiet investigative moments transition naturally into explosive action sequences without ever feeling forced. Every mission introduces new mechanics, locations, or scenarios that keep the experience engaging throughout the campaign. It understands that variety is essential for a spy adventure, and it delivers that variety **** soundtrack perfectly complements the atmosphere, blending orchestral tension with classic Bond-inspired themes. Combined with excellent sound design, it creates an immersive experience that constantly reinforces the feeling of starring in your own 007 movie.Perhaps what impressed me most is how confidently the developers established their own interpretation of James Bond. Instead of relying purely on nostalgia or imitating the films scene for scene, they crafted an identity that respects the franchise while giving it room to evolve. It feels modern without losing the sophistication, charm, and elegance that define **** only reason I didn't award it a perfect score has nothing to do with the game's quality. Simply put, spy-action adventures are not my favorite genre. If they were, I could easily see this being one of my favorite games of the year. Judging it purely on its own merits, it's an exceptionally polished, cinematic, and thoroughly entertaining experience.007 First Light proves that James Bond belongs in modern gaming just as much as he belongs on the big screen. It's stylish, intelligent, beautifully crafted, and consistently fun from beginning to **** outstanding spy thriller and one of the best adaptations the franchise has ever received.8/10

author: Wolveram
text: I really, really enjoyed 007 First Light. What impressed me most was the way the missions are designed and how seamlessly they integrate story and character development into the gameplay. I was genuinely surprised by how much I liked the characters and how attached I became to them over the course of the game. The story remained engaging and exciting from beginning to end.  Most importantly, the game absolutely captures the feeling of the best Bond films. Any concerns that the game might prioritize messaging over storytelling proved completely unfounded. At its core, this is a thrilling James Bond adventure. The mix of exploring sandbox-style levels, gathering intelligence, stealth gameplay, and transitioning into intense hand-to-hand combat and gunfights worked wonderfully for me.  I only have two major criticisms that keep this from being a perfect 10/10.  First, I experienced multiple crashes on my PS5 Pro, particularly during loading screens. While the game generally ran well, having to quit and restart several times was frustrating and occasionally broke the immersion.  Second, I'm increasingly bothered by the amount of handholding in modern games, and 007 First Light is no exception. Why does every climbable surface need to be marked with yellow paint? It feels like lazy game design. The constant button prompts are equally unnecessary. After vaulting over obstacles hundreds of times, I don't need another reminder telling me to "Press X to vault." Developers should trust players more and assume they can remember basic controls after the tutorial.  Those issues aside, 007 First Light was an incredibly fun experience. And that's exactly what I want from a 15–20 hour story-driven game. It's the kind of game I'll happily revisit every few years, and that's probably the highest compliment I can give it.

author: johnnystaps
text:
Let’s be entirely honest: if you strip away the 007 logo, the licensed music, and the Walther PPK, 007 First Light is a remarkably mediocre, generic action game.I’m genuinely baffled by the glowing praise this game is receiving. It seems like a massive case of "franchise starvation"—we haven't had a major Bond game in over a decade, and everyone is so desperate for one that the bar has dropped through the floor. Add in the immense goodwill critics have for IO Interactive after the Hitman trilogy, and it feels like people are reviewing the studio’s reputation rather than the actual game on the **** you went into this expecting the brilliant, open-ended sandbox freedom that IO is famous for, you are going to be severely disappointed. Here is why the "masterpiece" narrative doesn't hold up under actual scrutiny:

1. Heavily Scripted, "On-Rails" Boredom - The game sacrifices mechanical depth for cinematic choreography. It is aggressively linear and filled with restrictive scripting. When a spy game forces you through rigid Quick-Time Events (QTEs) just to handle basic narrative moments, it ceases to be an engaging stealth experience and becomes a playable movie.

2. Zero Stakes or Real Challenge - A great espionage game relies on tension. You should feel like an elite agent operating on a razor's edge. Instead, Bond can essentially stroll through high-security facilities with virtually no friction or threat. The AI is flat, the action feels entirely unrealistic, and the pacing is completely halted by clunky mechanics—like a combat system that forces you to wait for enemies to show "intent" before you can react naturally.

3. A Sci-Fi Identity Crisis - Bond works best when it's grounded in high-stakes, classic espionage. First Light veers way too far into generic tech-thriller/sci-fi territory with its focus on the THEIA supercomputer. It feels less like Ian Fleming or Casino Royale and more like a futuristic sci-fi shooter that lost its identity.

4. Check-The-Box Branding - The classic Bond staples are entirely skin-deep here. The Q-Lab feels uninspired and lame, giving you glorified keys for specific doors rather than clever gadgets that alter how you play. Worse, the "love interests" are completely hollow, dropped into the narrative without an ounce of chemistry just to tick a box on a developer checklist that says: "Look, it’s a Bond game!"

Final Verdict007 - First Light isn't a broken, buggy disaster, which is why it's getting safe, lazy passes from supporters. But being polished and shiny doesn't make it good. It is a shallow, rushed, on-rails experience that trades rewarding gameplay for cinematic window dressing. It’s an okay generic action game, but it is a terrible Bond game. Don't let the hype train fool you.

author: atlas007
text:
The game is "pretty good." My score is entirely for gameplay, but the visuals, voice acting, story, and so on, are all good to great. Bond's VA especially. 

But the gameplay...

1. Definitely nails the spy/espionage feel with the gadget mechanic. Gadgets involve resource management, which is great for combat but can be an unnecessary hinder to the spy puzzle solving when you've got to run around looking for charge/chemicals. A minor nuisance, but when the game gives you recharging resources it makes me think, "This would feel so much better as the norm..."

2. Combat is lacking though. In melee, parries are not satisfying or worth it because you only get the counter on the last hit, unless the enemy finishes with a grab in which case you cannot parry at all. Therefore.. just dodge all attacks/grabs and punish with your combos. The game gives you lots of options, but when dash attack, punch, gut punch, grab+slam either finishes or grants a takedown opportunity, it becomes repetitive.

3. Personally don't care much for the range of guns but the game not only gives you bullet time but also aim assist (even on "hard"). Not only that, you can just run around and enemies have very poor accuracy. I get that Bond films are full of action but some moments feel like a generic shooter game on easy.

Ultimately I had a good experience (despite it being quite buggy, experiencing a soft lock, crashes, and minor bugs but I'm forgiving a new release from a smaller developer) and would be open to the next Bond game hoping they make improvements. It was rather short though, about 15 hours.

text: First Light is a great introduction to what could become the next generation of James Bond games. It strikes a solid balance between espionage, action, stealth, hacking, and combat, keeping things fresh enough that the gameplay rarely feels repetitive. The story is engaging and does its job well, even if it’s not particularly memorable once the credits roll. One of the game’s strongest aspects is its progression system. The more you play, the more capable both you and Bond become. There’s a satisfying learning curve as you gradually master hand-to-hand combat, close- and long-range gunplay, stealth, and hacking. By the end, you genuinely feel like a skilled 00 agent who knows exactly what he’s doing. My biggest criticism is the level design. While the mission-based sandbox stealth/action game approach offers plenty of freedom within each mission, I often found myself wishing the game felt a little more open. Some environments can feel surprisingly restrictive and even a bit claustrophobic at times. Expanding the scale and giving players more room to approach objectives creatively would be a great step forward for future entries. That said, this is an incredibly promising start for IO Interactive’s new Bond franchise. Here’s hoping they get to keep their license to kill and continue building on this foundation in the next game.

author: TheMaritimeNerd
text: 007 First Light ReviewIntroductionJames Bond is a name that many gamers haven't heard in quite some time. In fact, it's been nearly 14 years since the last major James Bond game release in 2012. For those of us who grew up during the Nintendo 64 and PlayStation era, that's hard to believe. There was a time when it felt like a new Bond game arrived almost every ****, IO Interactive, the studio best known for the Hitman franchise, has accepted the mission of bringing the world's most famous secret agent back to gaming. But does 007 First Light successfully capture the magic of classic Bond games, or does it fall short of its target?Let's find out.StoryIn 007 First Light, players step into the shoes of a young James Bond before he becomes the legendary agent known as 007. Bond begins his journey serving in the Royal Navy, but during a mission, disaster strikes when his helicopter is shot down. As the sole survivor, Bond must fight his way through hostile territory and find a path to safety.While navigating the enemy camp, Bond receives assistance from Moneypenny, who guides him through the extraction process. Following his rescue, he is recruited into MI6's newly re-established Double-0 Program, beginning his transformation from an inexperienced soldier into one of the world's most skilled spies.Training plays a significant role in the early portion of the game, introducing players to Bond's future colleagues and mentor, Greenway. The training sequences feel like something straight out of an action movie, complete with montage moments reminiscent of classic films such as Rocky. It's entertaining, well-paced, and does an excellent job of establishing Bond's **** of the standout training missions places Bond in a nightclub where he must identify and make contact with a target among a crowd of agents. It's here that the game truly begins to embrace the spy fantasy, allowing players to utilize gadgets, deception, and intelligence gathering.However, once Bond enters the field on his first official assignment, things quickly spiral out of control. What begins as a routine operation evolves into a much larger conspiracy, forcing Bond to uncover dangerous secrets and prove that reviving the Double-0 Program was the right **** story delivers plenty of twists, memorable characters, and exciting set pieces while providing a compelling origin story for one of fiction's most iconic agents.GameplayTo make things easier, I'll break gameplay into five categories:•	Shooting•	Navigation and Stealth•	Gadgets•	Close-Quarters Combat•	DrivingShootingPrior to release, I had heard mixed opinions regarding the game's shooting mechanics. Some early impressions described them as merely average. After experiencing them myself, I completely disagree.Unlike action-heavy franchises such as Uncharted, Gears of War, or even some previous Bond games, 007 First Light does not rely on constant gunfights. Instead, combat encounters occur at specific moments and trigger what the game calls "License to Kill" sequences.During these encounters, Bond moves in and out of cover while engaging enemies in cinematic firefights. Environmental destruction plays a major role, allowing players to shoot explosive barrels, gas tanks, and pipelines. By activating Bond's Q Watch, players can identify environmental hazards and opportunities.Several combat abilities add depth to firefights. Bullet Time returns, slowing down time and allowing players to line up precise shots. Shooting enemies in the hands can disarm them, while leg shots cause them to stumble, creating opportunities for melee takedowns.Ammunition is intentionally limited, encouraging creativity. One of my favorite mechanics is being able to throw an empty weapon at an enemy, stunning them long enough to close the distance and finish them with a melee **** shooting may not be constant, but when it happens, it's exciting, satisfying, and highly cinematic.Navigation and Stealth007 First Light is a third-person action-adventure game, meaning players will spend a significant amount of time climbing, traversing environments, and exploring mission areas.Bond's movement feels very similar to Nathan Drake from the Uncharted series, and honestly, that's not a bad thing. Movement is smooth, responsive, and enjoyable throughout the **** game also provides multiple ways to approach objectives. If players prefer a more direct approach, they can use Instinct Points to bluff their way past guards by posing as authorized personnel. Instinct Points are earned through stealth actions, intelligence gathering, and eavesdropping on conversations.Alternatively, players can lure enemies away from patrol routes, perform stealth takedowns, or create distractions using objects such as radios and vacuum **** variety of options allows missions to feel flexible and rewards players for approaching situations creatively.GadgetsThis is where 007 First Light truly shines.

It’s a mystery to me why this game is so popular. From a game design perspective, I think it gets almost everything wrong. It plays like a game from more than ten years ago—yet it’s an inferior version of Uncharted 4, Hitman trilogy, Last of us or Detroit Become Human. 

All the driving sequences are completely superfluous and could easily have been cutscenes. They offer absolutely no added value to the gameplay. 

But the gameplay issues already start with the fact I can only throw objects directly at enemies. Why can’t I throw them elsewhere—like in real life, or to distract enemies the way you do in the much better Hitman Trilogy? Even without comparing it to Hitman, aren't I supposed to be a spy—or at least a human—who can throw objects anywhere to distract someone? Way less options than in other games and invisible walls everywhere—this game is very restrictive.

Generally, the whole game feels "on rails," as if I’m not even really playing it myself. There are zero stakes; most of the time, I just don't care—you simply blast your way through. The tools are way to easy to use you stop in front of some guy and shoot it at them unnoticed.

The thing is in a hitman game I feel like I wanna figure out one of the many options to solve the mission, I feel excited, there are stakes, there is thrill. In this game it takes you so much by the hand you dont even feel like you are playing it which results in you not being invested at all. I had to force myself to finish the game, and the longer I played, the more the missions felt like filler to stretch the playthough time.

The only good thing about it is the training montage right at the start, that’s a cool idea how it blends from one thing to another. It’s kind of funny, really: experienced players eventually get bored of games where you just shoot and beat up everything in sight via wild button-mashing, so they discover masterpieces like the Hitman trilogy—a relatively realistic agent simulation. author: JimmieD
text:
I think this game will polarize…
007 First Light is a breath of fresh air and one of the most enjoyable action-adventure games I’ve played in a while. 
The visuals are absolutely stunning, the Bond atmosphere is spot on and the game perfectly captures the charm, wit, and style you’d expect from 007. The combat feels impactful and exciting, and the variety of missions keeps things fresh throughout the adventure.

My biggest criticism is that the game can be a little too restrictive at times. Objectives are often marked immediately, leaving little room for exploration or figuring things out on your own. I was hoping for something a bit closer to Hitman, where you’re encouraged to investigate and experiment more. Some sections also feel extremely linear, and a frustrating boss encounter in the middle of the game briefly brought the experience to a halt by forcing a very specific approach instead of letting the player tackle it more freely.

That said, none of these issues were enough to seriously hurt my enjoyment. The game quickly regained its momentum afterwards, and the highs are simply too good to ignore. From start to finish, I had a great time. It’s stylish, varied, genuinely feels like James Bond and by the end I was already excited for a sequel. 

If I had one wish for the sequel, it would be for the devs to trust the player’s intelligence and creativity a little more. Give us more room to explore, investigate and approach objectives in our own way instead of immediately pointing us toward the solution. The foundations are already excellent, and a little more freedom could make the next game truly special, or in other words, a 10 out of 10.

Score: 8/10

author: MaleProtagonist
text: "James Bond Movies are for friends, so I don't need one."Honestly, don't let the 88 Metacritic score gaslight you. This is a classic case of style over substance. If you're expecting the peak sandbox freedom of the Hitman series, you’re really going to be disappointed. It feels more like Detroit: Become Human with occasional shooting sections than an actual stealth sandbox. Every now and then, the game teases player choice, only to shove you back onto the same scripted **** devs tried to create this ultimate gaming buffet, but they ended up watering down everything. It blends elements from Watch Dogs, Assassin's Creed, and Sleeping Dogs, but strips out all the depth. Most of the "freedom" is just the illusion of choice; you're just following highly scripted, contrived paths and hitting buttons when the game tells you to. There’s no actual "spy work" or genuine deduction here. Even Hitman: Absolution had a more satisfying gameplay loop and better controls than this, which is tragic.

author: Pickle
text:
I think it's a beautiful game.

Beautifully written, acted.

Beautiful gameplay, beautiful graphics, sound design.

I was quite cynical about the game when it got announced because I wondered how IOI would capture the essence of this character, but to my surprise they have done so perfectly.

The game has an awesome cast of characters, all of them serving different purposes to the main story, al well layered beyond the usual, this character betrayed you, this one didn't, type of twists and usual turns.

The gameplay is like a bit more powerful and melee focused Hitman, with gadgets that allow you to alter stuff around your environment and stun enemies. The focus very much isn't in just attacking enemies or shooting at them though; there's those moments, and those moments are handled well, but generally, this is a game that threads between all the things Bond does in films.

You're infiltrating, fighting, shooting, platforming, charming, all the while you're investigating and completing missions.

I was also concerned about the inclusion of some celebrities and influencers, but generally this is handled well and it comes off more charmingly & silly, rather than exploitative or tacky.

What I would criticize though is the focus at times. Like there's a wonderful mission where you're infiltrating with a partner into a building. At multiple points you're left to wonder how to open a locked door or reached a ledge. I would figure this stuff out but the game wouldn't let me actually interact or complete my goals until a set amount of time had passed and my partner mentioned the solution to me.

I remember God of War: Ragnarok being heavily criticized for spoiling the solutions to puzzles before you could figure them out. This does something similar, but in my opinion, more annoying; it waits till the NPC's spoil the solution in order to let you continue playing the game. It got quite annoying in that mission in particular, but thankfully it wasn't something that came up that much afterwards.

I also think the pacing can be a bit slow at the start and I don't like the - once again - arbitrary always online implementation for Tacsim mode. This is a mode you get after playing a while in the main story that lets you experiment with an escalation system similar to Hitman games throughout different missions in the campaign, the problem is that it is always online for... reasons... leaderboards? Maybe? I don't know... it has a challenge system and unlocks for suits if you're to complete each challenge of each mission, however, the unlocks INCLUDING THE PRE-ORDER COSTUMES can only be used in Tacsim mode........

These are the issues I've encountered with the game, but generally, speaking purely about the campaign. I think it's a memorable and beautifully crafted experience. It can be slow at times and it can be quite guided at times, and this last issue conflicts with the game's own incentive to try and play it your own way. But even then, it's a remarkable experience, despite these issues, the acting, writing, and the awesome set pieces and gameplay sequences, work for the most part in creating something truly special.

author: PMG-Writer
text: 007 First Light isn't a perfect game. The enemy AI is weak, technical issues prevent a flawless overall impression, and the gunfights don't quite reach the level of the excellent stealth mechanics. Nevertheless, IO Interactive has achieved something remarkable. The studio understands the DNA of James Bond better than many film adaptations of recent years. The gripping origin story, the flexible mission design, and the excellent espionage sequences truly make you feel like a budding 00 agent. Anyone who enjoys intelligent stealth games, thrilling spy stories, and classic Bond flair will find one of the most interesting action-adventure games of the year here. Not everything is perfect, but the direction is right – and it leaves you eager for more missions from this young James Bond.

Personally I feel like this game was front loaded in terms of quality to gain high review scores, but the second half of the game was abandoned. And let me state again. This is NOT a hitman game. author: Max9671
text: 007 First Light starts as a promising spy thriller, but it completely breaks its contract with the player. The developers spend the first half of the game forcing you to invest in relationships, character development, and a close-knit group dynamic. But just as you get attached, they abruptly rip the entire supporting cast away in a lazy, predictable plot device.What makes it unforgivable is how the game handles the aftermath. The narrative completely fails to give their deaths the respect, weight, or emotional acknowledgment they deserve. Instead, the game suddenly switches genres, abandoning its story entirely to become a hollow, mechanical checklist of generic spy tasks. Killing targets isn't a plot—it's just a gameplay loop. Once the emotional anchor is gone, the entire game feels empty, hollow, and utterly pointless.

Décevant quand on est vétéran des nouveaux Hitman et c'est peut-être mon erreur de trop le comparer à ces derniers. 

J'aurais aimé un plus large choix et conséquences dans la tournure des missions => le jeu nous fait croire qu'on à un semblant d'impact dans les choix de dialogues alors que pas du tout. 

Le choic de mettre des QTE n'est pas un problème mais pas assez exploité => ex: des actions secondaires comme regarder James jouer du piano sans utiliser des minis QTE donc soit on choisis d'en mettre ou pas du tout. 

Le côté Uncharted avec tous les rebords avec des fils ou draps jaune OSKOUR. 

Le fait de pouvoir bluffer est une super idée mais pareil pas assez exploité à mon goût. J'aurais aimé qu'au début des missions lors de notre briefing, que l'on doivent retenir notre couverture pour être mi au défis d'être un vrai caméléon lors des dialogues et mise en situation.

Les phases de shoot avec une multitude de barils rouges sont vraiment boring ainsi que les phases en véhicule, je comprends qu'elles soit présentes pour s'imprégner de l'univers des 007 mais vraiment pas fun.

Bref, 007 First Light n'est pas un mauvais jeu mais il est vraiment pas assez exploité dans ses mécaniques à l'inverse d'un Hitman qui pour moi est plus jouissif et intéressant à jouer et plus construit.

author: Sagraqui
text:
A MUST BUY for any gamer, not only Bond fans

007 First Light is an incredible Bond experience and, for me, a perfect game. I played it on PlayStation 5, and what impressed me most is how complete it feels: a long, cinematic adventure that plays like several great Bond movies in one.
The story is easily one of the best Bond stories I have experienced across film, books, and games. 
This younger version of Bond feels fresh: flawed, wilder, more human, and still learning how to become the icon we know. That makes the journey feel exciting and meaningful.Technically, the game is stunning.
 The lack of noticeable loading screens, the smooth transitions, the beautiful locations, and the strong performance make it feel like one continuous movie. 
The missions are varied, the gameplay allows room for combat, stealth, gadgets, and creativity, and every mission has its own memorable identity.
The visuals, music, art direction, and Lana Del Rey theme are all excellent.
 This is a love letter to James Bond fans, but also a must-play for anyone who enjoys cinematic action games, adventure shooters, stealth, or story-driven experiences.

007 First Light is not just a great Bond game. It is a game every player should experience.

author: Kenmei
text: I was a little hesitant about this when I heard it was being made by IO Interactive, who have basically only made 1 game over the past couple of decades with the Hitman franchise. I personally do not like Hitman at all due to it's janky nature and lack of depth to its story. Fortunately the story here is top notch, with great characters and a wonderful narrative that carry some of the gameplay issues it has here. I really enjoyed this being an origin story for Bond, something we never really have gotten before. It's fairly well done, even if Bond becomes a Gary Stu towards the end to justify some of the decisions he makes. But I was gripped from the beginning and it lasted all the way to end of the 10ish hour campaign. Knowing it's part 1 of a trilogy too makes me very excited for the future games to come here. Unfortunately it's gameplay still fall into the janky category for me. While it's been polished up from the Hitman series, its still an issue controlling and fighting with Bond. Plus this has to have some of the dumbest enemy AI I've seen in many years. Frankly it's horrible and needs a ton of fine tuning for the next game. But the story is good enough to cover for some of those issues and I now can't wait for the next one in the series and where they'll go from here.

author: StyzzaGaming
text:
007 feels a lot like “0047 First Light,” and that works in its favor. The sandbox design, social stealth, and creative assassinations will feel familiar to Hitman fans, with added cinematic flair and Bond gadgets.

When it clicks, it is genuinely fun. Sneaking through crowded spaces, navigating levels, and pulling off clean takedowns all feel satisfying. The visuals, music, and pacing do a lot to sell the fantasy of being a junior spy.

It is not consistent. Combat and gadgets feel clunky at first and take time to settle. Some sections drag, with too much time spent slowly searching for ledges, crawlspaces, keycards, or hidden panels. The launch issues did not help either. Crashes and lost progress forced me to replay hours, and even though stability improved, that stuck with me.

The real problem is the product placement. It is constant and impossible to ignore. Bond is always tied to specific brands, from his watch to his cars to the environments around him. It stops feeling like part of the world and starts feeling like advertising. Paying $70 while being pushed ads aggressively breaks immersion and leaves a bad taste. 

The core gameplay is strong, but this is where I draw the line. Because of the product placement, this is a not recommended, and I will ramp up my efforts to be aware of product placement in games before purchasing in the future.

author: goldzweig
text:
It’s a game that doesn’t take risks; it plays it safe, and if you’ve played Hitman before, this is basically it. Nothing revolutionary here, and it doesn't feel fresh at all.    

Setting & Exploration: The atmosphere is great, and the levels are highly detailed and fun to explore. However, there were only a few missions where I actually enjoyed this.    

Combat & AI: The combat is pretty shallow, and the gunplay is very simple and easy. The AI is dumb as a brick; at no point did I think, "Holy sht, that was clever, I didn't even see that guy flanking me."* It’s incredibly easy to stay alive in this game.    

Story: For those who enjoy 007 movies, the story is really cool. It's a bit predictable, but it felt like watching a new James Bond movie.    

Pacing: To artificially extend the game's length, they throw a bunch of filler BS in the middle just to waste your time. They could have given the player more freedom.    

Gameplay Formula: The approach to solving challenges follows the exact same formula the entire game: you get close to people talking, press Y, and listen to them say something so you can get a clue and progress. This holds the player's hand way too much; it could have been less guided. Other than that, you just scout the people around you, grab a keycard, and move on to the next section.    

Replay Value: Replay value is non-existent. Once you beat the game, you’ve seen it all. It made me wish there were multiple story paths depending on how you complete a mission. That would actually make me want to replay it to see the rest. Heck, maybe even new levels that you couldn't access in a single playthrough. (Like The Witcher 2, where if you side with the elf, you go to one area, and if you side with the human, you go to another—and there's no way to explore both in one run).

Summary: If you’re a 007 fan, go for it. If you’re not that into it, the best part—which is the story—won't make much of a difference to you.

Also, it was surprisingly buggy for me on the base PS5. Tons of controller issues, janky combat, character stuck on terrain, one hard crash, and some terrible stuttering at later sections of the game.

Perhaps I hyped myself up too much, but in the end I found myself rushing to finish it just to get it over with, sell my copy, and play something else. I have no desire to replay it. Maybe IO can polish over those rough areas for the sequels, we’ll see. 

For now this is a 6/10 at best for me, maybe a 7/10 if I’ve had some coffee.

author: faaifuipeuaidjb
text:
Disappointing considering what IOI are capable of producing. 

I appreciate this is not a Hitman game, but they could have taken more from that series and applied it here. 

For example, in Hitman you have a location and within that are all the resources and intelligence available to complete your objective; then it's up to you to figure it out. 

First Light, however, is so on-rails you never really feel like you're in control. There was one segment I recall where guards denied entry to an area - but the camera immediately pans to an air vent that the player character happens to be standing right next to. You're not really given the chance to work stuff out for yourself. 

The driving sections are largely pointless as there's nowhere to go other than where the game is pointing you - they may as well be cut-scenes with no player interaction. 

There are other annoying elements, too - guards will have infinite ammo but drop weapons with 2 rounds in them. Combat could do with a camera lock or enemy focus option, as sometimes Bond will end up facing away from combat altogether. 

There are positives - the story is solid and very on-brand, the characters are well done, the environments look great, and the sound design is very good too. I loved the movie-montage style training that forms the tutorial. 

It's sadly just very boring to play - I find myself wishing that they'd just re-skinned Hitman and placed that game into these locations.

author: fuqyoudrewskiii
text:
A Masterclass in Action-Espionage: 

007 First Light is an absolute triumph and easily one of the most incredible gaming experiences I’ve had in years. IO Interactive hasn’t just made a great Bond origin story, they’ve set a new high bar for the action-adventure genre. Playing this on a PS5 Pro paired with a 65" LG C4 OLED takes the presentation to an entirely different level.

The Good:

• Phenomenal Story & Pacing: The narrative is gripping from start to finish. It anchors you perfectly into this younger, building version of Bond, making you feel the weight of his journey to earn that double-0 status.

• Industry-Leading Combat: The combat is arguably the best I’ve ever played in a third-person game. It is fluid, aggressive, and highly improvisational, even outpacing heavyweights like Assassin’s Creed that are entirely built around physical engagement. The environmental takedowns and parry mechanics make every single brawl feel incredibly rewarding.

• Incredible Attention to Movement Detail: One of my favorite details is the sheer fluidity and accuracy of the character movement. When Bond walks up or down stairs, or navigates uphill and downhill terrain, his feet and body adjust perfectly to the slope. A lot of modern AAA games skimp out on this kind of animation detail, but here, it adds an immense layer of grounded realism to the exploration. 

• High-End Character Visuals & Display Performance: By and large, the graphics are stellar. The facial animations capture a fantastic level of nuance and emotion, and the hair textures are remarkably detailed. On the LG C4 OLED, the contrast and ink-black levels make the dark, stealth-heavy environments look stunning, while the PS5 Pro keeps the overall image incredibly sharp and responsive.

The Flaws: 

• Inconsistent Texture Polish: While the major visual presentation is gorgeous, there is a noticeable lack of polish on certain environmental textures. Because the LG C4 and PS5 Pro deliver such a sharp, clear picture, it actually makes the occasional low-resolution textures in main, highly trafficked areas stand out a bit more, briefly breaking the immersion. 

• Early Stability Issues: The game did hard crash on me during the very first mission's opening cutscene. Fortunately, performance was rock-solid after that initial hiccup with zero crashes since, but it’s worth noting for launch-week stability.

Final Thoughts: Minor texture seams and a singular day-one crash can't derail what is ultimately a masterpiece. If you have the hardware to push it to its limits, it's a visual treat, but even baseline, the gameplay makes you truly feel like Bond. This is an absolute must-play.

author: phoenixprjct
text:
First Light delivers an exceptional origins story of a young, reckless James Bond brought to life with hearty charm by Patrick Gibson in a sleek, action-packed tale of identity, artificial intelligence, and conspiracy that puts many a silver screen outings to shame. IO Interactive leverage their expertise in player freedom to craft a controlled but flexible third-person adventure with stunning set pieces designed to make the most out of their gameplay concoction of stealth, combat, and spy craft.

Some rough spots come from trying to squeeze in as much Bond goodness as possible, but it’s hard to hold it against the game too much. Overall, First Light is a cinematic but engaging action-adventure game that balances player control with bombastic spectacle, proving IO Interactive were very much the right choice to break the pall that has lingered over the franchise’s gaming exploits over the last decade.

So, from at least me, I’d say IO Interactive’s license to continue killing it with instalments is more than granted…just don’t make the experience so bumpy with as many parts as Hitman, please?

author: niko433a
text:
007 First Light – 7/10

I'm giving 007 First Light a light 7/10. My main enjoyment came from the story, which kept me engaged throughout the game. However, almost everything else felt fairly mediocre.

The open-area exploration, clearly inspired by the recent Hitman games, feels underdeveloped. Most objectives boil down to "go here, press a button, then go somewhere else and press another button." There are very few opportunities for players to creatively use their gadgets or approach situations in their own way, which is disappointing for a game centered around a spy like James Bond.

The melee combat is particularly rough. It often feels janky and unresponsive, and enemies can attack so quickly that countering them becomes frustrating rather than rewarding. Gunplay is serviceable, but nothing special; it gets the job done without ever standing out.

Overall, while the story provides a solid reason to see the game through to the end, the gameplay lacks the depth and polish needed to make 007 First Light truly memorable.

Also, their checkpoint system seems to be messed up when you try to return to a checkpoint; it goes back to a completely different checkpoint instead of being in the current area you are in

author: JaidenMC
text:
The name’s Bond. James Bond.

When this game was first announced in 2020, I wouldn’t even know what to really expect from this game, except all I knew that I knew it was going to be an awesome experience coming from one of my other favorite developers of all time, IO Interactive (shortened as IOI), known their groundbreaking and innovative assassination sandbox that is the Hitman franchise.

After a long 5 1/2 year development cycle, and with an ambitious scope after developing one of my favorite games of all time, Hitman 3, the question was that is this game that people would hoping it would be like Hitman meeting some bits of Uncharted?Well, I can immediately say that this game immediately brought back the legacy of Bond and delivered a fantastic first adventure with the iconic spy agent from start to finish.Really fantastic combat, that gives me Arkham and classic Yakuza vibes, gunplay that is reminiscent of Uncharted, story’s very strong, really well acted, pretty cool stealth mechanics that’s easier than Hitman, and despite some frame rate hiccups, a bit of a slower pacing, and some annoying sections while in combat, First Light feels like the start of something big that IOI is building up to and absolutely delivered on what it sets out to do.

Gibson’s portrayal of the iconic Bond is fantastic and the animation in the facial expressions and environment is really impressive and unreal to look at, and this game is a reminder that the Glacier engine is one impressive piece of technology and continues to get better and better with more titles from IOI.

007 First Light, is nearly perfect. It’s an awesome first time experience for IOI’s take on Bond and captured the essence of what makes 007 a pretty cool and fun experience for spy enthusiasts all around the world. This game to me gets a 9.5 out of 10. Truly an awesome first time and next step for IOI as both a developer and for their 007 games going forward. Super good.
