text: Pur presentando un intreccio tutto sommato interessante e avvincente, seppur fin troppo reiterato nel genere spy-action, First Light pecca decisamente dal punto di vista tecnico e di gameplay. Nel primo caso, in modalità prestazioni, la qualità delle textures è ormai di almeno cinque anni fa, con una grana pellicola fin troppo densa, atta a mascherare l'arretratezza delle textures, analogamente alle animazioni dei **** (incluse le animazioni facciali), ancorate oramai alla generazione precedente di console che, in tale ottica, non può assolutamente giustificare i cali di frame nelle situazioni più concitate o con un numero elevato di NPC, specie tenendo presente la natura lineare del gioco. Dal punto di vista del gameplay, il gioco si pone quale compromesso tra Hitman, prodotto della stessa software house di 007 e Uncharted, non riuscendo a raggiungere, purtroppo, i picchi di nessuno dei due: le possibilità di accesso sono molto più limitate rispetto a quelle dell'Agente 47, limitandosi il più delle volte a distrarre alcuni NPC e raccogliere chiavi d'accesso, ecc... con uno stealth estremamente inquadrato e fondato sul distrarre l'arretrata IA la quale, durante le fasi di shooting, appare più che predisposta a ricevere un headshot, risultando quindi affine a quella di Hitman, tollerabile per quest'ultima tipologia di gioco, ma non per un action. Infine, il prodotto soffre di gravi problemi di ritmo e ripetitività, dato che ciascuna missione è schematizzabile in: briefing, individuare la modalità d'accesso all'area protetta, fase stealth di infiltrazione, cutscene con il villain di turno, eventuale bossfight e fase di shooting con una pletora di sagome da poligono di tiro. In sostanza, si tratta di un prodotto nella media, che non innova nulla nel suo genere e che ripropone dinamiche consolidate ormai da almeno dieci anni, non riuscendo a proporre un comparto tecnico all'altezza di giochi in terza persona e lineari, anche non attuali

author: chrolloprudo7
text: It would have made for a perfect James Bond movie. The game perfectly captured every element of a James Bond film. I found the characters, in particular, to be very fitting. The Bond Girls were perfectly designed, and I was also very fond of the protagonist. What made the characters feel even more alive was the excellent facial motion capture; every subtle facial expression was captured, resulting in much more expressive dialogue and cutscenes. Both the dialogue and the narrative choices were solid—mostly quite humorous, though that didn't bother me at all. Next, we come to the game's greatest strength: its atmosphere and locations. It truly felt like watching several James Bond movies back-to-back. The range of settings was incredibly diverse, spanning everywhere from Vietnam to England. Exploring these locations was particularly enjoyable, though it did occasionally feel a bit repetitive. The balance between action and exploration was very well-executed. Quick Time Events (QTEs) appeared more frequently during the early stages of the game than they did later on; it would have been cool if that intensity hadn't tapered off. The infiltration mechanics also became somewhat repetitive, but the parkour and climbing sequences helped redeem those repetitive moments to some extent. In general, I really enjoyed the climbing mechanics—they felt very smooth. Speaking of smooth, both the HUD and the overall gameplay felt incredibly fluid. The combat reminded me of *Sifu* (in fact, the controls were even partially identical). The gunplay was also very satisfying, though I found myself running out of ammo quite quickly, which forced me to pause the gunplay briefly while I scrambled to pick up a new weapon. In terms of both combat and exploration, the gadgets were pretty cool—though I ended up using the laser and the dart gun most frequently.A few of the boss fights could have been designed a bit better, and I found the online system to be rather annoying. On a lighter note, the trophy names were pretty cool—they were all references to the titles of the James Bond films! My final point would be the game's performance. I experienced virtually no frame drops, except in the world section. And the ray tracing almost knocked my socks off—it was practically perfect.

author: Prestigiousss
text: This might be one of the best action adventure games I've ever played. A straight 10/10 experience from beginning to end. 007 First Light doesn't just capture what makes James Bond special, it fully embraces it and delivers the ultimate interactive Bond fantasy. From the opening mission to the final credits, I felt like I was starring in my own blockbuster spy film. The gameplay is where this game truly shines. The developers somehow managed to combine the best elements of Hitman and Uncharted into one seamless experience. On one hand, you have the freedom and creativity of a spy thriller where planning, infiltration, and stealth are rewarded. On the other hand, you have the cinematic set pieces, action sequences, and thrilling escapes that make every mission feel like it belongs in a Bond movie. What I loved most was the freedom of choice. Nearly every situation allows you to decide how you want to approach it. You can sneak through an area unnoticed, carefully taking down enemies and gathering intelligence. You can go in guns blazing and rely on your shooting skills to survive. Or you can mix both approaches together depending on how the mission unfolds. The game never forces you into a single playstyle, and that flexibility makes every mission feel exciting and replayable. The combat and fighting mechanics are also fantastic. Whether you're exchanging gunfire, engaging in hand to hand combat, or improvising during intense encounters, everything feels fluid and satisfying. The melee combat especially stood out to me because it feels impactful and cinematic without becoming repetitive. Every fight feels like something straight out of a James Bond film. The presentation is absolutely top tier. The visuals are stunning, the locations are breathtaking, and every mission feels larger than life. From glamorous high society events to dangerous enemy strongholds, the game constantly puts you in iconic Bond situations. The attention to detail is incredible, and the world feels authentic from beginning to end. The story is exactly what I wanted from a James Bond game. It delivers espionage, action, intrigue, betrayal, and memorable characters while maintaining the sophisticated charm that defines the franchise. It strikes the perfect balance between being a thrilling spy adventure and a personal journey for Bond himself. And I have to give special recognition to Lana Del Rey because she absolutely nailed the theme song. Her voice perfectly captures the elegance, mystery, and emotion that have always defined the best Bond themes. The song instantly felt iconic, and honestly, I'd love to hear her contribute to more movies in the future because she was the perfect choice for this soundtrack. What impressed me most is how cinematic the entire experience feels. Every mission, every action sequence, every conversation, and every set piece feels like you're playing through a major Hollywood production. It never loses sight of what makes James Bond special, and because of that, it succeeds on every level. It's rare for a game to perfectly blend action, stealth, storytelling, freedom of choice, and cinematic presentation, but 007 First Light somehow accomplishes all of it. For me, this isn't just a great James Bond game, it's one of the best action adventure games ever made.

author: Aszach
text: 007 First Light is easily one of the best James Bond games Ive played. It does a fantastic job of making you feel like a spy while still delivering satisfying action throughout the entire campaign. The biggest highlight for me was the combat, especially the melee combat. Every fight feels smooth, fluid & responsive, and taking down enemies up close never gets old & as for the gunplay, it's still good, but like most shooting games on a controller. The mission design is also excellent. Many objectives can be completed in different ways, whether through stealth, gadgets, or direct action, which gives players a lot of freedom in how they approach situations. The characters are another strong point. I found many of them memorable, and they helped keep me invested in the story from beginning to end. Visually, the game is also impressive, featuring a great variety of locations, from open outdoor areas and laboratories to office buildings and snowy mountain environments. The constant change in scenery keeps the adventure feeling fresh. My main complaint is that the game is too short. I also found the game surprisingly easy, even on Purist difficulty. Because enemies rarely pose much of a threat, I often found myself brute-forcing encounters instead of fully utilizing the gadget system. The gadgets are fun, but the lack of challenge means there's not always a strong reason to use them. Despite those issues, 007 First Light is an excellent spy action game with great combat, strong mission variety, memorable characters, and fantastic environments. I only wish it were longer and more challenging.

author: Holycrazia
text:
This game is an absolute masterpiece. The gameplay, the story, the pacing—it’s all just spot on. It completely nails the James Bond vibe; you truly feel like you are 007. I was entirely immersed for the roughly 15 hours it took me to complete the main story without doing tacsim, and I haven't had this much fun with a game in a very long time. I’m already looking forward to playing it again.

The way the social stealth blends with the action is brilliant. It feels like Uncharted married Hitman and had a child. The combat and shooting feel fantastic—never frustratingly hard, but never too easy either.

If you're looking for downsides, there are very few. I ran into a couple of bugs that required a reload, and the graphics might not be quite on par with the absolute best-looking titles on the market, but it gets close. Honestly, those are minor nitpicks.

I will be recommending this game to everyone. I truly hope it gets the massive success it deserves because the developers knocked it out of the park.

Thank you for three nights of undeniable fun, IO Interactive!

author: Tubey
text:
007 First Light is a game of contradictions. On a surface level, it's a very passable action game that pays good tribute to the source material, keeping the narrative flowing and not overstaying its' welcome. 

On the flipside, it's overly streamlined, extremely easy even on the hardest difficulty settings, has absolutely woeful driving segments and stilted combat.

It feels like a movie that reluctantly has gameplay sections. It's by no means bad, I enjoyed it, but the critic scores are clearly over the top - but then critics enjoying a game you need zero skill to play isn't exactly a new phenomenon.

My advice would be to wait for a sale and treat it like you would a rental game back in the day - good for one playthrough, something you won't regret playing but you'll forget about soon enough.

author: Voodoo123
text:
Mutch like the relic that is the James bond franchise, io interactives sterling effort feels like game design from the past often coming off like a "true crime" meets "stranglehold" meets "sleeping dogs" and even some of the jankiness of "enter the matrix". Wheras the latter carried the charm of being entirely new ip carving its own path in a dead sea of mario , GTA 3  and cod clones this outing carries the burden of high expectations often framed by talking heads as being an uncharted like AAA single player powerhouse. 

This is not what I found. Greetings to glitching ai that aften causes guards in fully rendered tac gear only to be seen walking into walls going nowhere or sitting on invisible chairs. Add in a generic forgettable plot about ai.Generic sounding underwhelming bond casting/accent/choice for a younger aged bond.Frustrating game design that doesn't feel as open as hitman or as "free flowing linear" as uncharted.Terrible driving sections feel awful too. Constant on screen interruptions saying "cannot connect to online server" even though it's a single player game. Non sensical resource system has your cinematic hero scrounging for washing conditioners and phone batteries to enable shoot a laser or knockout dart? Very long load times ps5 pro. Overused trope where character constantly knocked out only to load into cutaways for next gameplay/cut scene must've happened at least 25+ times across the play through no joke. 

Minute long unskippable title cards/safety notices etc each time you boot the game from dashboard. Distracting (almost) last gen like screen space based lighting artifacts are constantly distracting the eye.Poor HDR implementation results in less contrast than it should. Soft looking final image in spite of using 5 pro pssr2. Distracting near constant texture/lod swapping near player view. No manual save, checkpoint system seems random sporadic often had to replay the previous 15+mins gameplay as punishment when I chose"restart checkpoint" was just trying to listen to an alternative dialogue option I had selected by mistake. 

Positives now and witty banter can be very fun. Some of the combat sequences played out well with the explosive sections of scenery to create excitement. Overall thoughts so far are it's a good effort that comes across like a lesser hitman game with some uncharted esque influences that are poorly executed when you compare to uc4. 

I enjoyed io interactives good effort here and if you're on the fence, might be worth purchasing once it's found it's way to the bargain bin but I couldn't justify the current price to you outside of sheer enthusiasm that this is what you might want to try. Hopefully the tech issues I found will be patched over the games lifespan.

author: LuxPlay11
text:
Incredible James Bond, best of the series by far. Starting from story, all the way to the combat. Other than usual day one issues like some minor glitches or game crashes, I haven't encountered any larger issues that can be seen with a lot of other games in recent times.

With game being built on Glacier engine (same one that powers Hitman World of Assassination, as well as older version powers Kane & Lynch) has once more proven to be powerful and equally open engine. By combining stealth elements from Hitman (although changed and adapted to this genre) as well as their knowledge of how to make a combat game from times of Kane & Lynch  (and well from the ever so disliked Hitman Absolution) has been combined into making this game as perfect as is. Some will say quite the opposite from me, but getting a game as polished, prepared and ready for release in 2026 is a hard job and a rare sight at that.

Going over to more "creative" part of the game, voice acting. Voice acting is superb, accents fit all the characters (looking at Hitman with limited accents as to oppose this one) as well as surprisingly large variance of voices for NPCs (looking at you Watch Dogs Legion), as well as amazing voice acting even for the lesser side characters like Monroe and Cressida.

At side of mechanics, I was concerned how that would play out and I must say I was shocked. From incredibly well thought-out hand-to-hand combat, gun play and the Q-watch mechanics have made me feel like I was James Bond and I was in the game. Q-watch was integrated in game with such detail that some parts of the game are near impossible to finish without it and it's not just a fun gimmick, and they managed to make it not feel like it's being stuck down your throat at that.

Yes, the game is linear, but so are their previous levels from previous IO games. The game features a robust replay menu, being able to start from nearly any point in the mission or just from the beginning and that adds extra layer of the openness to the game. Following in footsteps of Hitman once more, each level has at least half dozen different ways to reach the target location or accomplish a certain goal, offering hours of replayability and that certain feel of "branching linearity". Personally I feel that an open-world James Bond game would not work, James Bond isn't the type of person to run from point A to point B to grab certain things and missions, his missions are always time sensitive and have clear goals.

Considering the length of game at around 15 hours, some criticise it for being too short, however I believe in quality over quantity. As seen in some recent games with longer playtime, the added playtime just amounts to filler content that would make replaying the game tedious or just downright difficult at time.

Overall, it is my opinion that is going to be one of, if not the best game of 2026 (only game that could possibly top it is upcoming GTA VI, but that would be more of size) and it is incredible to see that a medium sized Danish developer that was in crisis in 2018 following loss of their partnership with Square Enix, come back even stronger and release the best Bond game of all time, and all that with "only" 200 million dollars of game budget.

author: gabe_needle
text:
Wow, wow!
Après environ 8 heures de jeu, je peux déjà dire une chose : James Bond: First Light est un gros potentiel GOTY 2026.

L'histoire est complètement nouvelle, repensée. Comme dans les films de James Bond, il y a plein de mystères, de twists et de rebondissements. Honnêtement, je suis tellement impressioné par le gameplay que j'en oubli que ce sont les créateurs des Hitmans qui l'ont fait. ( Hitman c'est bien, mais très clunky niveau contrôles.)

Côté gameplay, c'est probablement ce qui m'impressionne le plus. J'ai vraiment l'impression de jouer à un mélange entre Hitman et Uncharted. Tu peux être discret, infiltrer des endroits, utiliser des gadgets, puis quelques minutes plus **** te retrouver dans une grosse séquence d'action digne d'un film.

Pour les graphismes, je joue sur un PC haut de gamme avec une très bonne télé. Est-ce que ce sont les plus beaux graphismes que j'ai vus cette année? Non. Mais est-ce que c'est beau? Absolument. Les environnements sont détaillés, les personnages sont bien faits et tout roule super bien. Je donnerais facilement un 7.5/10 aux graphismes.

Là où le jeu frappe vraiment fort, c'est au niveau de l'ambiance. La musique, la mise en scène, les dialogues... tout te donne l'impression d'être James Bond. Pas juste de contrôler un personnage dans un jeu vidéo, mais vraiment d'incarner un jeune 007 à en devenir. C'est probablement ce que le jeu réussit le mieux. Un arrogance charmante, un trouble de l'opposition classique chez Bond. On a la chance d'incarner un gars de 26 ans qui malgré lui n'a aucune idée de la carrière et les challenges qui se préparent.

Patrick Gibson incarne avec brio le jeune James. J'avais deja trippé sur son jeu en tant que jeune Dexter dans la télé-série. Il est parfaitement à sa place et les personnages secondaires sont tous intéressants. Après seulement quelques heures t'es déjà attaché à eux.

Le plus gros compliment que je peux faire au jeu, c'est que je viens à peine de le commencer et je suis déjà un peu triste de savoir qu'il va finir dans un douzaine d'heures.(campagne de 20 heures environ.)

Ça fait longtemps qu'un jeu ne m'avait pas donné ce feeling-là. J'ai déjà hâte à une suite.

Pour moi, c'est un solide 9,5/10 jusqu'à présent. Une expérience vraiment incroyable et facilement une de mes plus belles surprises de l'année, parce que disons le, les previews étaient très , très moyens.

author: Hrotbertus
text:
007 First Light had immense potential. 
Exploring the origins of entertainment's most famous secret agent, backed by today's technology, should have been an absolute triumph for the gaming industry. Instead, we are looking at yet another major casualty of a sterile, destructive contemporary trend. It is a forced reimagining that, in its clumsy attempt to pander to damaging and pointless modern hypersensitivities, ends up irreparably disfiguring and compromising a legendary character, and the statements made by the production team were sadly prophetic. At the end of the day, they feel like a slap in the face to anyone who actually knows and loves the franchise. Claiming that an "old school" James Bond is "tone deaf in this day" and masking the systematic dismantling of the character behind the rhetoric of "reflecting modern values" is an exercise in pure authorial arrogance. Associating "old school" with something negative is just absurd. They promise fans that the agent will retain his seductive charm, reassuring the audience that "beautiful women are there" (thank god, at least there is that) and that Bond "has got game", but it is all just a facade.Beneath the surface, the result is a sanitized and entirely flat protagonist filtered through the lens of ideological conformity, an approach that devolves into ridiculous, pointless, and harmful moralizing, stripping the game of its edge rather than adding any real depth. The pretentious question of "what does it take to save the world in 2026?" to justify stripping away the character's defining traits is not evolution: it is simply capitulating to a restrictive mindset.This title is the perfect embodiment of a broader sickness, a trend that is systematically ruining the entertainment world in all its forms, and gaming is no exception. The problem plaguing the industry, which First Light captures perfectly, is twofold. On one hand, you have major studios stubbornly failing to grasp, or worse, deliberately ignoring reality: the overwhelming majority of the audience simply wants to enjoy a work of fiction for what it is. Gamers are looking for escapism and immersion, and they want to be represented by strong characters who stay true to their core nature, without being subjected to constant moral lecturing or having historic icons clumsily rewritten just to avoid offending anyone (and honestly, who is even getting "offended" and by what?). Only when industry executives finally realize that normalcy and the actual demands of the market lie elsewhere, will we go back to getting products with genuine narrative integrity. On the other hand, there is a bitter truth regarding the audience itself: a significant portion of the player base passively accepts these shifts, consuming products with zero critical thinking or completely ignoring the bigger picture. It is exactly this lazy compliance that allows companies to get away with these approaches, validating the destruction of historic franchises. Making matters even more bitter is the technical side of things. And here lies another massive regret, because the graphics in 007 First Light are genuinely beautiful, finally looking good and fully worthy of the PlayStation 5. While not a flawless masterpiece, it is the only aspect of the game where the word "modern" actually makes sense to use. Despite that vocal minority of critics and players who stubbornly downplay the importance of visuals, proving they do not understand what technology, realism, and immersion truly mean in modern gaming, the graphics here prove to be absolutely fundamental. It is just a shame that the developers wasted such an impressive visual engine to deliver such a compromised creative vision, proving they should have focused their mental energy entirely on the technical execution, leaving the soul of James Bond well enough alone.

author: JayPenrith
text:
As you can see I do not often review but I felt I had to this time, not long after you take your first tentative steps into First Light, when it becomes absolutely clear that IO Interactive has not merely made a good James Bond game. They have made the definitive James Bond game. Possibly the best Bond experience in any medium since the franchise's golden era.

The premise is inspired. This is an original origin story, following a 26-year-old James Bond, a promising but occasionally reckless Royal Navy air crewman who catches the attention of MI6 and finds himself recruited into the newly revived 00 programme. It sounds straightforward on paper, but the execution is anything but. The story that unfolds from that foundation is layered, surprising, and genuinely gripping from beginning to end.Patrick Gibson is an absolute revelation in the lead role. He has the considerable advantage of a twenty-hour game rather than just two hours of film to develop the character, and he uses every minute of it. 

This is a Bond who feels real, flawed, charming, and worth caring about. He earns the number. You believe every step of the way, gameplay is where IO Interactive truly flex their craft. Their years building the Hitman franchise have prepared them perfectly for this moment. The stealth systems are deep and satisfying, but what sets this apart is how it wraps all of that in unmistakable Bond DNA. This is not a cold, clinical assassin. This is a charismatic spy who talks his way into restricted areas, improvises under pressure, and always manages to look good doing it. The social stealth missions in particular are some of the finest levels in recent gaming memory, with enormous sandboxes and an almost overwhelming number of ways to approach any given objective. You can play it loud, or you can play it smart, and both feel completely valid, supporting cast gives the whole production genuine cinematic weight, and the production values throughout are frankly staggering. This looks and feels like a Bond film that just happens to also be interactive. 

Then there is the theme song. Lana Del Rey has finally got her Bond song, and she has made it count. Co-written and composed with the legendary David Arnold, "First Light" is a slow burner that reveals its full emotional depth only as you settle into the world of the game. When it swells across that title sequence, it stops you cold. It is elegant, atmospheric, and unmistakably Bond, the kind of track that sits comfortably alongside the very best the franchise has ever produced. It was worth the wait. After fourteen years without a Bond game worthy of the name, IO Interactive has delivered something genuinely extraordinary. This is the game Bond fans have been waiting for. A love letter to the franchise, a triumph of game design, and frankly one of the most enjoyable experiences you will have in front of a screen this year. Do not miss it.

author: IamBedman
text:
First release I preordered in a while. And never regretted it in the 12h I played through the main campaign. 

Gameplaywise, the IOI formula of levels being a completely open Sandbox is working perfectly in tandem with the toys you get. You WILL know the basics of a load of those if you played Hitman but/and the Bluffing is a decent mechanic to add to that toolbox. The limit in Insinct, Chemicals and Electricity may seem too strict at the very first, but the more you get the hand of the gadgets and mechanics, the more naturally you'll flow between them and with little time you'll have organically developed your own kind of "Attack Flow". And all of that perfectly immerses you into the story it wants to tell if you let it.

The characters are nice, especially the Bond. Patrick Gibson really nailed the role. I dont want to spoiler it tho.

Technic side is the only -1 for me. I played on a regular PS5 using Performance Mode. I did encounter some low detail textures not loading into high res, but those were rather rare. The more pressing ones are one full game crash, rather sparingly set Checkpoints in a game that cannot be manually saved (or I was too dumb to find the button) and, by far the worst of all, a couple of server disconnects. The latter being a huge annoyance and if you know how they handled that in Hitman or how Square Enix did it in JC3, you know why but if you dont... wherever you are or whatever you're doing, once the servers are lost, the game gets forced into a pause and will remain on full hold until the complete reconnect is done. That should be moved into the background of things. The servers are not that important. Doing automatic background reconnects should very much be possible and would greatly increase the experience overall.

author: Freeger2789
text:
I’ve been a long term Hitman player & fan.

It is simply a technical marvel. Years of massive work were put into the game, and I can see the complexity and details at every step. The programming of the AI, vehicles, water, interactive objects and situations — must have been insanely complex, considering the driving mechanics simply lacked in Hitman. The story is massive and takes hours to complete (it really does feel like progressing through a movie — but you’re the main character), but overall it is worth it — and it is well written and the action is fast-paced. The culturally diverse backgrounds, the presence of multiple languages — including the details of levels, the reactions of NPCs, even the dried rain stains on glass or the design of the euro banknotes or the electrocution of NPCs — all overwhelmingly accurate — is what did it for me. I loved the Finnish brothers part. Honestly, my family thought that it’s a movie at first. Easily one of the best games in the year 2026 and beyond — no other James Bond game has ever reached this level. Bravo, IOI. I sure do hope the next Hitman games or other IPs will adopt these mechanics. I’m honestly surprised all NPCs react to you bumping into them — it only makes the world more realistic, alive and complex. 

Lastly, I love that enemy NPCs now know how to flank you. Yes — they flanked me hard and formed a perimeter and I died. Scandalous. They also draw weapons in rare, contextual/special cases which makes it even more realistic — it gives you a window to fight until chaos ensues.

P.S. Romanian subtitles missing were me doing the hard work of translating British puns and charming lines to my brother. After all, I paid the full price and pre-ordered it — to catch up on my English class. And yes, I went with hard mode — so reloading checkpoints basically became my favorite task.

author: Lanckakhter
text: I honestly didnt expect this game to hit me THIS hard.I waited for this game for months because I love James Bond movies, especially Daniel Craig era, and somehow this game actually made me FEEL like Bond more then some of the movies themselves.This is not just "another action game". The whole vibe is insane. From the intro, the music, the MI6 base, gadgets, betrayals, conspiracies, missions, all of it just works together perfectly. There were multiple moments where I literally sat there thinking "holy **** this is exactly what I wanted from a Bond game".What surprised me most is how cinematic everything feels. The game reminds me of Uncharted sometimes with the huge setpieces and pacing, but also Hitman with stealth and freedom in missions. But it still has its own identity. It doesnt feel like a copy.I LOVE how the game slowly builds Bond into the legend instead of making him a perfect super agent from the start. The whole beginning with training and becoming the last surviving 00 agent actually made me care about the story and character way more then I expected.Also one thing that I absolutely loved:you are not just running around shooting everyone. The game actually makes you feel like an AGENT. Sometimes you cant even use your gun until things go completely wrong and someone pulls a weapon first. Then suddenly you get that "license to kill" feeling and the gameplay changes completely. Its so damn **** honestly? The story got me hard. The feeling that MI6 basically leaves you alone, that you are outside the system trying to uncover a huge conspiracy while only a few people still trust you... thats PEAK James Bond for me. It felt exactly like those Daniel Craig movies where Bond always ends up isolated and has to fix everything himself.I played around 20 hours total because I didnt want to rush it. I literally stopped before the ending because I had work in 2 hours and I didnt want to experience the finale tired or half focused. Thats how much I cared about this game by the end.Only negatives for me:car crash/chase sequences felt weaker then the rest of the gameplay and I wish weapon customization was deeper, especially suppressors because its Bond after **** yeah, I understand why some people think 70 dollars/euros is expensive. It IS expensive. But I also think people forget inflation exists. Just because AAA games cost 60 dollars 10 years ago doesnt mean they can realistically stay the same forever while budgets become insane.Back then many huge games cost like 20-30 million to make. Now games like this use full performance capture, hollywood level cinematics, massive teams, licensed IPs and budgets that can hit 200-300 million dollars. People say they want big cinematic singleplayer games and sequels, but at the same time dont want these games to actually make enough money to survive and get future parts.Honestly I would rather pay 70 for a polished memorable experience like this then spend 100 hours in some bloated boring open world full of filler **** Interactive seriously cooked with this one. Please let this game sell well because I NEED a sequel.

author: m_mkhaimer
text: 007 First Light on PS5 is nothing short of a masterpiece. From the very first mission, it delivers the ultimate James Bond fantasy with unmatched style, cinematic storytelling, and breathtaking action. Every second feels polished to perfection, making it one of the greatest PlayStation 5 experiences ever **** graphics are absolutely stunning. The game pushes the PS5 hardware to its limits with ultra-realistic lighting, detailed environments, and smooth performance that never misses a beat. Whether you’re sneaking through a high-security facility in the snow or speeding through neon-lit cities in a luxury Aston Martin, every scene looks like it belongs in a blockbuster Bond **** gameplay is flawless. Combat feels smooth, satisfying, and incredibly dynamic. Stealth missions are tense and rewarding, while the explosive action sequences create nonstop adrenaline. The controls are responsive and intuitive, making every gadget, weapon, and hand-to-hand encounter feel powerful. The DualSense features add another level of immersion — every trigger pull, explosion, and car chase feels alive in your hands.What truly makes 007 First Light special is its atmosphere. The soundtrack is phenomenal, perfectly capturing the classic Bond vibe while feeling modern and epic. The voice acting is exceptional, and the writing is sharp, witty, and emotionally engaging. Bond himself is charismatic, confident, and effortlessly cool throughout the entire **** missions are incredibly varied and creative, constantly introducing new mechanics, locations, and set pieces that keep the experience fresh from beginning to end. Every chapter raises the stakes higher, making it impossible to put the controller down.This is not just the perfect James Bond game — it is one of the best action games ever made. 007 First Light combines cinematic storytelling, incredible gameplay, stunning visuals, and pure entertainment into one unforgettable experience. author: IzaMxReal
text: The hype surrounding 007: First Light was massive. With mainstream critics pushing review scores near perfection, the game promised to deliver the ultimate secret agent experience. However, after diving deep into it, the reality is entirely different: this game is a stark reminder that the current industry prefers financing dazzling graphics over innovative mechanics or realistic physics.Here is a deep, realistic analysis of why those high scores fail to justify a product that is, at its core, remarkably mediocre.1. The "Frankenstein Effect": A Total Lack of IdentityFirst Light invents absolutely nothing; it simply loots the closets of well-established franchises. The platforming and linear action sequences are a stripped-down carbon copy of the cinematic formula found in Uncharted, while the stealth elements, gadgets, and environment manipulation feel like direct structural recycling from the Watch Dogs series.Borrowing mechanics that work is not a crime, but the real issue here is that the game fails to add a single layer of its own depth. Lacking identity, the title feels less like an artistic vision and more like a generic product packaged under a famous brand. It works, sure, but in a completely flat and predictable way.2. Cutting-Edge Graphics vs. Twenty-Year-Old PhysicsThe game looks stunning at first glance thanks to impeccable lighting and high-resolution textures—which seems to be exactly what bedazzled the gaming press. But that photorealism **** into pieces the moment you interact with the world.A flagrant example of this is the environmental destruction. When shooting or knocking over shelves and structures, the debris magically vanishes after a few seconds instead of remaining on the ground. This lack of object persistence completely destroys immersion and any sense of realism. In this day and age, sacrificing dynamic physics and environmental interactivity just to maintain a stable frame rate is an unacceptable technical shortcut for a game aspiring to excellence.Conclusion: A Technical Pass, an Innovation Fail007: First Light is not a technical trainwreck, but it is a mediocre game when it comes to its mechanics. It is a title designed in a marketing lab to be "safe and marketable," relying on visual smoke and mirrors to cover up its lack of detail and zero **** you are just looking for eye candy to showcase your hardware, it delivers. If you are looking for a game that respects your intelligence and brings something fresh to the espionage genre, you can safely skip it.

author: BatNurse
text: Just 20 minutes in and this feels like a proper cinematic 007 movie. Graphics look beautiful most of the time on PS5 Pro. I have noticed some jagged shadows and pop in for objects out in the distance but nothing too jarring and honestly I would be really impressed if this game didn't have some visual hiccups with how good everything looks and feels. You can tell the Hitman DNA is all over this with it's sandbox style approach to missions. This is the best iteration of it in my opinion and geniunely makes you feel like a spy. There is definitely some bugs but the overall gameplay and structure is so good I can easily overlook the technical issues that will hopefully be ironed out in future patches. The gameplay and missions are some of the best and most immersive i've experienced in a single player game. Stealth is done beautifully and choosing your gadgets opens different opportunities for you to take advantage of during your missions. Hand to hand combat is awesome and reminds me of how smooth and realistic feeling TLOU Part 2 is. There is an entire second game mode aside from the main story that features hitman like simulations with plenty of unlockables and reward structure. Ultimately there is some technical issues that I noticed occasionally, some games are hindered by this but 007 First Light is so masterful in every aspect it becomes a non issue. Fantastically epic and fun set pieces this game feels like a 007 movie with the world class sandbox level design of the Hitman Series makes this a true contender for GOTY.
